what.text: This page follows refugees from the Democratic Republic of the Congo living in Namibia, as counted by UNHCR at the end of each year.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 4839 refugees from the Democratic Republic of the Congo in Namibia, 0.4% of all refugees from the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
Uganda hosts the most refugees from the Democratic Republic of the Congo, followed by Burundi, Zambia and Rwanda.

why.text: UCDP records armed conflict over the government of DR Congo in periods from 1996 to 2025, with M23 among the opponents.
It also records armed conflict with the Islamic State group from 2017 to 2025.

when.text: UNHCR's series for this group starts in 1993 at 6 refugees.
The figure is at its highest at the end of 2025, and the main years of displacement in the data are 2019 to 2025.

how.text: The sources don't say which routes people took or where they live in Namibia.
These are year-end totals for Namibia only, reported to UNHCR.
